header: THE THIRD SET OF TRAINS OF THE PAID RAILRADAR MONTH: THE TRAINS THAT START AT HOWRAH, SEALDAH, SANTRAGACHI OR KOLKATA AND GO OVER NEITHER DURGAPUR NOR ASANSOL. The first two sets are in the database already (trains that stop at Durgapur or pass it without stopping; trains that go over Asansol but not Durgapur). The owner asked for the rest of the trains of the Kolkata terminals, "mutually exclusive": a train that touches two of the four stations is taken once, from its STARTING station. What I take, in the owner's words made exact:

* A train is IN the set when (1) it STARTS at one of the four (HWH Howrah Jn, SDAH Sealdah, SRC Santragachi Jn, KOAA Kolkata) and (2) its route does not go over Durgapur (DGR) or Asansol (ASN), whether it stops there or not.
* It is taken ONCE, whichever boards it is on, under its starting station (a Howrah train that stops at Santragachi is on both boards and counts as a Howrah train).
* A train that merely ENDS at one of the four, or passes it, starts elsewhere and is not "from" these stations: it is not in the set (its fare would be from another station).

HOW I KNOW WHAT GOES OVER DURGAPUR AND ASANSOL, two ways that must agree: (a) the station boards of Durgapur and Asansol with includeIntermediate=true, which list the halts AND the pass-throughs; (b) the train's own full route (GET /v1/trains/{n}, every station it goes through, halts or not), read for every train of the set before anything is asked for its fares. A train that is on either board, or whose route has DGR or ASN, is OUT, with its reason kept. This file holds the pure rules (no request, no database), so that they can be tested on the real answers of 28 Nov 2026.

symbols.name: TERMINALS
symbols.sig: const TERMINALS = [ { code: "HWH", name: "Howrah Jn" }, { code: "SDAH", name: "Sealdah" }, { code: "SRC", name: "Santragachi Jn" }, …

symbols.name: EXCLUDED_STATIONS
doc: The two stations whose trains the owner already has: a train that goes over either is not in this set.

symbols.name: parseBoard
symbols.sig: export function parseBoard(json: unknown, code: string, minTrains = 10): BoardRow[]
doc: Reads a station board (GET /v1/stations/CODE/trains?includeIntermediate=true). Anything that is not that shape is an error: a half-read board would put wrong trains in or out of the set.

members.name: touches
doc: Which of the four stations' boards the train is on (it is taken once, under `from`)

symbols.name: selectCandidates
symbols.sig: export function selectCandidates(boards: Record<string, BoardRow[]>, passing: Record<string, BoardRow[]>): { candidates: Candidate[]; rejected: Rejected[] }
doc: THE SET BEFORE THE ROUTE CHECK. `boards` are the four terminals' boards, `passing` the boards of Durgapur and Asansol (with the pass-throughs). Each train that STARTS at one of the four is taken once; those on a Durgapur or Asansol board are out with the reason. A train that is not for passengers (a parcel express) is out too.

members.name: classes
doc: the classes the train has, as RailRadar lists them ("availableClasses")

members.name: route
doc: every station code on the route, halts and the rest, in order (to prove it does not go over DGR or ASN)

symbols.name: parseTrainFull
symbols.sig: export function parseTrainFull(json: unknown, number: string): TrainFull
doc: Reads a train's full record (GET /v1/trains/{n}?haltsOnly=false): its details, its halts with times, and every station of its route. It must be the train asked for, with a start station and a route.

symbols.name: goesOver
doc: The route proof: which of Durgapur and Asansol the train goes over (empty when neither).

symbols.name: hasReservedFares
doc: A train gets fares from the reservation system when it can be booked there (isPrsBookable); suburban and local trains cannot, so they keep their details and have no fare. NOTE: the classes the train's own record lists are NOT enough to say which classes to ask for: checked on 28 Nov 2026, the Howrah - Barbil Jan Shatabdi (12021) lists CC only and the fare service sells 2S on it too (the other three trains tried matched). So the classes are found the way the Durgapur set's were: all eight asked for the fare to the END of the run, and the halts in between are asked for the classes that answered.

symbols.name: reservedClasses
doc: The classes the record lists, for the budget only (the real classes are found at the end station).

symbols.name: haltsOnlyJson
doc: The halts after the starting station, as parseSchedule (fare.ts) reads them: a copy of the answer that holds only the halts (and reversals).

symbols.name: requestsFor
doc: An estimate of the requests a train's fares need: all eight classes at the end station, then one per listed class (at least one) for each halt in between. A train with no reserved fares needs none.

behaviours: the addresses ask for the boards with the pass-throughs and for the full route
a board that is not the answer expected, or holds too few trains, is an error and never half a set
every train of the set STARTS at one of the four stations, each once
a train on two of the four boards is taken once, under its starting station: the Howrah - Pune Duronto (on Howrah's board and Santragachi's) is Howrah's, touching both
the Coromandel Express, which Santragachi's board also has, is Howrah's too, once

trains that start at Sealdah, Santragachi and Kolkata are there under their own stations (Darjeeling Mail SDAH; Sealdah - Puri Duronto SDAH; the Santragachi - Tambaram Antyodaya SRC; Kolkata - Guwahati Garib Rath KOAA)
a train that only ENDS at Howrah (the Howrah SF Express from Tiruchchirappalli, the Howrah Mail from Mumbai) is not in the set, and not 'out' either: it does not start there
trains on the Durgapur or Asansol board are out with the reason: the Howrah Rajdhani (12301) and the Howrah - Ranchi Shatabdi (12019)
no train of the set is on either the Durgapur or the Asansol board
a parcel train (Jpp Rcs Express 00150) is out: not for passengers
the Howrah - New Jalpaiguri Shatabdi and the Howrah - Gaya Express are in the set before the route check (their routes are what proves it)
the full record of 13023 gives its details: Howrah - Gaya Express, HWH to GAYA, 654.6 km, daily, returning as 13024, classes 2A, 3A and SL, bookable
its halts are the 36 halts with their km from Howrah (0 at Howrah, 107.2 at Barddhaman, 654.6 at Gaya), the route holds all 142 stations, halts or not
the route proof: 13023 goes over neither Durgapur nor Asansol (it goes by the Sahibganj loop), so it stays in; the same route with Durgapur put into it is caught, and one with Asansol too
the classes the record lists are known (Sleeper, AC 3 tier, AC 2 tier) and the train has reserved fares
the estimate of its fares' cost: all eight classes at the end station, then the listed classes for each halt in between: 8 + 3 x 34 = 110

a train that cannot be booked in the reservation system (suburban, local) has details and no fares, and costs no request; one that can be booked is asked, whatever its record lists (12021 lists CC and the fare service sells 2S on it too)
the halts after the starting station read by the same reader as the Durgapur set's: 35 stops, Barddhaman at 107.2 km, the last Gaya at 654.6 km
a record that is not the train asked for, or has no route, is an error
the catalogue row of a train in the set keeps its halts; one that is out keeps none and says why
a saved row reads back the same, and one that is not a train number is refused
the three tables are made closed to the public roles (row-level security on, rights taken from anon and authenticated)
the SQL file for the tables names the same three tables
